newsitem.title: UK: Loud music deafening a generation - report.
newsitem.headline: Loud music deafening a generation - report.

text.p: Up to a quarter of young Germans have damaged their hearing by listening to loud music, New Scientist magazine reported on Thursday.
One in 10 of the country's 18-year-olds may have suffered damage severe enough to handicap them in normal conversation, according to a separate research study.
The results have prompted German officials to propose Europe-wide limits on the volume of personal stereos.
Researchers at the Institute for Occupational Medicine at the Heinrich Heine University in Duesseldorf examined 1,800 men aged between 18 and 24 at military recruiting centres around the country.
They found some hearing loss in about a quarter of them and also discovered that the recruits with poor hearing were more likely to have spent time listening to loud music.
In a second study by the government's Federal Environmental Office, researchers examined the listening habits and hearing of 270 students in Berlin.
They found that nearly 10 percent of students aged between 16 and 18 had lost so much of their hearing that they had difficulty in understanding some normal conversation.
Despite the German findings, New Scientist reported some scepticism among other researchers, who had failed to find similar hearing damage among youngsters in Britain and Sweden.
